title: SAT Ratios, Rates & Unit Conversions: Every Question Type and Trap
description:
Ratios, rates, and unit conversions are one of the official Problem-Solving and Data Analysis skills on the digital SAT. They look easy, but the questions are built around a few very specific mistakes. This lesson covers every way the skill is tested, with six SAT-style practice questions that get harder as you go.

You'll learn:
• How to set up a proportion so it can't come out upside down
• Part-to-part vs part-to-whole ratios (the 4 : 7 trap)
• Dimensional analysis: chaining conversion factors so units cancel
• Rates in mixed units (per hour vs per minute) and combined work rates
• Why square yards and cubic yards don't convert by 3, and what to do instead
• Scale drawings, maps, and population density
• A 4-step test-day method

All practice questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Problem-Solving and Data Analysis → Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units).
